title: Commuting squares for evaluated triangle composites
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a scheme $S$ with $\ell$ invertible, a finite level $n+1$, and a presentation $p$ with maps $d$ and etale-origin comparisons $h$. For every SingleLevelComparisons $c$ [def-sp-tower-p1-single-level-data], put $a_L=c.push_L$ and $b_H=c.pull_H$. For all bounded-below etale $L$ on $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ and $H$ on $S$, the specified composite words satisfy $\nu_S^*(F_n\eta_{n,L};\varepsilon_{n,F_nL});a_L=a_L;e_n(F\eta_{J_PL};\varepsilon_{FJ_PL})$ and $\nu_P^*(\eta_{n,G_nH};G_n\varepsilon_{n,H});b_H=b_H;e_n(\eta_{GJ_SH};G\varepsilon_{J_SH})$, where semicolon denotes composition in diagrammatic order. Neither tower composite is assumed to equal an identity, and this statement asserts no triangle identity.

proof.text:
Use [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] for the natural comparisons $e_nF\simeq Rq_{*,B_n}e_n$ on pro-etale categories and $e_nq_ ullet^*=q^{-1}e_n$, and for compatibility with tensor, composition and the specified adjunction-mate maps. Apply [lem-sp-tower-p1-etale-origin-comparisons] to pass, on etale-origin levels, to the corresponding ordinary etale operations through the specified comparison mate. Substituting $e_nJ_{n,P}=
u_P^*$ and $e_nJ_{n,S}=
u_S^*$ yields natural isomorphisms $a_L:e_nFJ_{n,P}L\simeq
u_S^*F_nL$ and $b_H:e_nGJ_{n,S}H\simeq
u_P^*G_nH$. Twists and the shift $[2]$ are included in that cited compatibility. The cited comparison lemma also says that $F,G$ preserve the displayed bounded-below etale-origin domains. Hence it applies again to $FJ_{n,P}L$, $GJ_{n,S}H$ and their iterates. Compose its natural comparisons to obtain those for $FG$ and $GF$. This uses only the level witnesses just constructed, not a compatible choice of etale representatives for a general tower; the cited lemma imposes no finite-Tor hypothesis.

source.place: Levels, final paragraph; single-level test objects for the finite triangle identities

proof.text: Under these comparisons, $e_n\eta_{J_{n,P}L}=\nu_P^*\eta_{n,L}$ and $e_n\varepsilon_{J_{n,S}H}=\nu_S^*\varepsilon_{n,H}$, with the respective source and target identifications understood. Indeed [lem-sp-tower-p1-etale-origin-comparisons] explicitly identifies the evaluations of the diagonal and splitting-trace formulas, including inverses of the projection/exchange isomorphisms, twists, shifts and the composition identification $p_i\Delta=1_P$. For the unit this is the word consisting of the composition identification, inverse supported projection, $Rp_{2*}(\delta\otimes1)$ and inverse exchange; for the counit it is inverse projection followed by $1\otimes t_q$. Evaluation preserves composition and sends an inverse isomorphism to the inverse of its image, so the entire words, not just their objects, are identified. The same assertion applies with input $FJ_{n,P}L$ or $GJ_{n,S}H$. Naturality in their chosen witnesses supplies exactly the conjugations by $a_L,b_H$ required for the iterated formulas.

theorem singleLevelTransport (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsUnit (l : Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (p : Presentation l E S hS) (d : Maps l E p) (h : EtaleOriginComparisons l E p d)
    (c : SingleLevelComparisons l E n d h) :
    (∀ L : DerivedCategory.Plus
        (Sheaf (ProjectiveLine S).smallEtaleTopology
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (levelRing l E n))),
      (nu l E n S).map
          ((singleLevelF l E n S).map
              (singleLevelEta l E n c.coordinates h.cartier_diagonal L.obj) ≫
            singleLevelEpsilon l E n c.coordinates ((singleLevelF l E n S).obj L.obj)) ≫
        c.push.hom.app L =
      c.push.hom.app L ≫ (SpTowerShriek.Ev l E S n).map
        ((p.F l E).map (eta l E d ((c.projective.J l E n).obj L)) ≫
          epsilon l E d ((left l E d).obj ((c.projective.J l E n).obj L)))) ∧
    (∀ H : DerivedCategory.Plus
        (Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (levelRing l E n))),
      (nu l E n (ProjectiveLine S)).map
          (singleLevelEta l E n c.coordinates h.cartier_diagonal
              ((singleLevelG l E n S).obj H.obj) ≫
            (singleLevelG l E n S).map (singleLevelEpsilon l E n c.coordinates H.obj)) ≫
        c.pull.hom.app H =
      c.pull.hom.app H ≫ (SpTowerShriek.Ev l E (ProjectiveLine S) n).map
        (eta l E d ((rightRestricted l E d).obj ((c.base.J l E n).obj H)) ≫
          (p.G l E).map (epsilon l E d ((c.base.J l E n).obj H))))
